topic: Bayes' Theorem: The Geometry of Changing Your Mind
target_audience: University students or advanced high school students with a basic grasp of probability

sections.title: The Core Intuition: Probability as Space
lecture_lines: Imagine all possibilities fit inside a unit square.
The total area of this square equals one.
We represent probability as a specific area within it.
animations: Draw a square outline (#FFFFFF) and fill with dark grey (#333333).
Fade in label 'Area = 1' (#FFFFFF) at the square's center.
Turn 10% of square blue (#3498DB) with label 'Event' (#3498DB).

sections.title: The Scenario: Prior Probabilities
lecture_lines: Meet a robot detective hunting for a Glitch-Bot.
Only twenty percent of bots in this factory glitch.
We split our square to show this prior belief.
animations: Divide square vertically: 20% red (#E74C3C) and 80% green (#2ECC71).
Label red region 'Glitch-Bot' [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg] and green region 'Normal-Bot' [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg].
Pulse the 'Glitch-Bot' label [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg] (#E74C3C) to emphasize the prior.

sections.title: The Evidence: Conditional Likelihood
lecture_lines: The detective uses a Spark Test on a bot.
Ninety percent of Glitch-Bots spark when tested.
But ten percent of Normal-Bots also spark.
We slice the rectangles to show these likelihoods.
Shaded areas represent the chance of seeing a spark.
animations: Shade top 90% of red region brighter red (#FF5555).
Shade top 10% of green region brighter green (#55FF55).
Label bright red 'True Positive' and bright green 'False Positive'.
Dim lower regions of both rectangles to near-black (#111111).
Highlight horizontal 'slicing' line (#FFFFFF) separating sparking from non-sparking with [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/detect.svg].

sections.title: The Geometric Update: Slicing the Universe
lecture_lines: Suddenly, the robot detective sees a bright spark.
Non-sparking possibilities are now impossible in our world.
We discard the bottom sections of our probability square.
Our universe shrinks to only the shaded regions.
Only two possible paths to a spark remain.
animations: Flash the 'Spark' areas (#FF5555 and #55FF55) brightly.
Fade out near-black 'non-sparking' regions to black (#000000).
Slide the remaining top blocks down to the baseline.
Shift 'True Positive' and 'False Positive' blocks together.
Draw a white brace (#FFFFFF) under blocks labeled 'Total Evidence'.

sections.title: The Posterior: Re-normalizing the World
lecture_lines: We must find the new probability of a Glitch-Bot.
Compare the Glitch-Spark area to the total spark area.
We stretch these remaining areas to fill the square.
This re-normalization reveals our updated posterior belief.
The Glitch-Bot probability is now roughly sixty-nine percent.
animations: Scale height of both blocks to fill the original height.
Scale widths proportionally so total width equals original square width.
Change 'Glitch-Bot' slice color to bright gold (#F1C40F) and display the robot icon [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg].
Display posterior percentage '69.2%' (#F1C40F) inside gold region.
Highlight the boundary (#FFFFFF) between the two final regions.

sections.title: From Geometry to Formula
lecture_lines: This geometric process is exactly what Bayes' Theorem describes.
The numerator represents the specific shaded Glitch-Spark area.
Dividing by the total shaded area gives the posterior.
animations: Display the equation P(H|E) = [P(E|H)*P(H)]/P(E) in white (#FFFFFF) while incorporating the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/glitch.svg] icon to emphasize the complex calculation.
Box the numerator and point to the gold area (#F1C40F).
Box the denominator and point to the entire width (#FFFFFF).
